name: planned
description: Use when the outcome is already decided and what remains is deciding how to deliver it. Plan (manual gate) -> implement -> review, which chooses by the nature of its findings whether to send the branch back for revision or the approach itself back to plan -> PR, with a human reading the review verdict before it opens. If the product direction itself is still open, route to research first. Skip the plan gate when the shape is already obvious enough to just build (shaped).

stages.name: plan
stages.description: Planning agent studies the task and records the implementation plan; the human reviews it before advancing
stages.prompt:
$TASK_PROMPT

If the ledger context this session started from shows you were re-entered here through the review stage's "replan" exit, this is a revised-plan visit: record the revised plan as your result, and on that same kanna_complete_stage call also pass `expected_definition` (the workflowDefinition read from kanna_get_task) and `workflow_definition` (the identical document — the existing "in progress", "review" and "pr" stages kept byte for byte; a replan revises the plan, not the shape) so this task's remaining plan is formally replaced through the T1 remaining-plan replacement contract, and confirm `workflowExtended: true` in the response. On the workflow's first entry (not a replan), record the plan as usual with no `workflow_definition`.

stages.name: in progress
stages.description: Agent implements the approved plan; the transition commits its work

stages.name: review
stages.description: Review agent checks quality and coverage, choosing the revision target by the nature of the findings, before the human reads the verdict
stages.prompt: Review branch $BRANCH against base $BASE_REF. This workflow routes results by named exits, not kanna_request_revision (which this task refuses for agent-origin calls). Record your verdict with kanna_complete_stage: status "success", your findings as the message, and an exit chosen by the nature of the blocking findings: "revise" for implementation defects, back to "in progress" as usual; "replan" when the approach itself is structurally wrong — the plan cannot produce a correct result however well it is executed — back to "plan", framed as what the revised plan must address. A pass is status "success" with no exit, which advances to pr once a person confirms it. Never call kanna_request_revision on this task.

stages.name: pr
stages.description: Agent creates a GitHub PR and hands off to the merge master
stages.prompt: Create a PR for the reviewed work on branch $BRANCH.
